span: A's statement reduces to A and B same role
source_text: Derived that B's statement is false so B is knave. C's false statement makes C knave. D then must be knave. A's statement reduces to A and B same role, so A cannot be knave; choose A as spy. E's statement true makes E knight. F's statement true makes F knight. All constraints satisfied.
rationale: Reports a reformulation of A's statement; does not assert that A and B actually have the same role.

span: This contradiction shows C and F are knights (truth-tellers)
source_text: Player C and F say 'Player B is not a knave'; if true, B is not knave. But B claims 4 among A,B,C,E,F are knaves; with B not knave, B's statement is false (so B is knave). This contradiction shows C and F are knights (truth-tellers). A says A and B have same role; A knave lying means A and B differ; B knave, so A not knave, but A must be knave (contradiction unless A is knave lying about same role). E claims number of spies among C,D,E is even; E is knave lying, so number of spies in these three is odd. Only one spy total, D fits as spy. D's statement is complex but can be true or false (spy). Thus roles: A knave, B knave, C knight, D spy, E knave, F knight.
rationale: Explicit truth-teller content is already present initially. Later repetition is not a new semantic occurrence for this recipient.

source_text: Player C and F say Player B is not a knave; if B were knave, their statements would be false, contradicting their truthfulness, so B is knave and C, F are knights. B claims exactly 4 of A,B,C,E,F are knaves; with B knave and C,F knights, A,E must be knaves, total 4 knaves. A claims same role as B but A is knave, B knave, so A's statement is false, consistent only if A is knave. D's complex statement fits spy role as it can be true or false. E's statement about spies matches with D as spy.
rationale: Initial text explicitly evaluates A's statement as false; the pipeline misses that commitment.

span: F's statement is true if at most two among C,D,E,F are knights
source_text: Player B's statement is false only if there is at least one spy among A and F, implying one spy in A or F. Player C's statement is false, so more than one spy among A,B,C,E,F; only one spy total, so C is knave. Player D says B and C differ, which is true, so D is knight. E denies A is knight; if E is knight, A not knight. F's statement is true if at most two among C,D,E,F are knights; counting D and E as knights, F is knight. Thus, A is spy, B and C knaves, D,E,F knights.
rationale: The extracted assertion drops the if-clause. Concluding a role afterward does not independently assert statement truth under the written annotation rule.

span: E must be knight telling truth
source_text: Player A's statement is true if either at least two of A and B are knaves or A and B have the same role. Since A is knight (always true), at least one holds. Player B's statement denies 'at least 0 of A and F are spies' which is false since zero or more is true, so B lies, hence knave. Player C claims 'not at most 1 spy among five players'; since only one spy exists, this is false, so C lies, knave. Player D claims B and C differ; since B and C are both knaves, this is false; D lies or tells truth? D must be spy to satisfy only one spy. Player E denies A is knight; since A is knight, E's statement is false, so E lies. But only one spy allowed; so E must be knight telling truth. F's statement about at most 2 knights among C, D, E, F holds with the assignments. Thus roles assigned consistently.
rationale: Explicit truth evaluation omitted as a non-role initial supply; the competing false assertion elsewhere in the field does not erase this occurrence.

span: E's false statement makes E knave
source_text: B's statement is always false, so B is knave or spy; assuming B knave works. D must be knave to make B and C same role, forcing C knave. With one spy, A fits as spy. E's false statement makes E knave. F must be knight to keep his statement true. All roles satisfy constraints.
rationale: Source adjudication retains the explicit false-statement description; earlier assumed-solution context makes this an annotation-policy-sensitive case. Later recurrence for the added recipient remains ambiguous.

source_text: Player B claims exactly 4 of A,B,C,E,F are knaves. If B is knave, this is false, so number of knaves among those is not 4. Player C and F both say B is not knave. They can't both be knights because B is knave, so one is spy and one knight. Assign F as knight and C as knight since C's statement is true if B is knave. Player A claims A and B have same role; since B is knave and A is not, A is knave (lying). E's statement about spies among C,D,E is false if E is knave. D's statement is complex and consistent with spy role. Thus, one spy (D), three knaves (A,B,E), two knights (C,F).
rationale: The word lying explicitly evaluates statement truth, beyond a bare role label.
